lesson_title: Design a Tower Nobody Minds Looking At
hook_text: Five hundred millimetres of card, straws and string. It must hold 200 grams, survive a shove, and not ruin the view.
clip_script: A settlement outside Rustenburg has no signal. Write the brief: who needs it, what you will make, who it is for, and one way to spare the view. Then specifications with numbers: at least 500 millimetres tall, base inside a 150 by 150 square, holds 200 grams, top moves under 10 millimetres when pushed, comes back upright, under 150 grams of material, every face triangulated. Now plan where it would fail and fix it in advance. Corners turn: glue triangular webs into them. Glued points fail: gussets across every joint. Panels lean: an X on every face. Faces braced but the tower still twists: string pulled tight through the inside, corner to opposite corner. Finally the view. Dress it as a tree, a flagpole for the school, a wind pump on the horizon. But a canopy adds weight up top, so make the base stronger to pay for it. Brief, numbers, reinforcement, disguise. Now you are ready to sketch.
visual_style: Whiteboard brief filling a box, then a tower outline with webs, gussets, X's and an internal string appearing where arrows point; a card canopy drops on and the base thickens.
mood: Organised and ambitious, the project snapping into focus.
pacing: Brief and specifications in brisk beats, four failure-and-fix pairs, the disguise twist with its cost.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write your tower brief and specifications tonight.
